s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, with imaging showing a well-defined, lobulated, and hypodense mass
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the left medial thigh
Firm, nonpulsatile mass fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
Well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass on CT scan with internal septations and density similar to subcutaneous fat
key_facts: 18-month-old girl
Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass enlarged gradually over six months
Painless mass
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass
Mass measures approximately 10 cm
Fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
CT scan showed a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass
Mass exhibited internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat
MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations

shortlist.label: Lipoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, painless, and firm mass in a child, with imaging characteristics of a well-defined, lobulated, and hypodense mass

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign tumor that can present as a firm, nonpulsatile mass, although the size and location are less typical

shortlist.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare in children, it can present as a slowly growing mass, and the imaging characteristics are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a firm, nonpulsatile mass, and the imaging characteristics of a well-defined, lobulated mass are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a firm, nonpulsatile mass, although the imaging characteristics are less specific for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The mass is a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense lesion with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, which is consistent with lipoblastoma, a rare benign tumor that typically occurs in children and is composed of mature and immature fat cells.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipoma is less likely as it typically does not exhibit internal septations and is less common in this age group

rejected.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
rejected.why: Myxoid liposarcoma is a malignant tumor that is rare in children and typically has a more aggressive appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma is a benign tumor that involves the nerves and is not typically described as a well-defined, lobulated mass

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: Angiolipoma is a benign tumor that is typically smaller and more painful than the described mass
